_doc: The Arduino Mega 2560 Rev3 (ATmega2560, 16 MHz) as the kit's streamer uses it to drive up to eight stepper axes, each on an external driver: the pins are the streamer's choice, read against the core's pin table. Its outline is community until measured. Board in the x-y plane.
name: arduino-mega-2560

step_pin_s0.rule: Axis 0's STEP to its driver: port A bit 0 (PA0), so the streamer steps all eight in one write
step_pin_s0.source: The kit's streamer, arm.ino (built for the Mega), which chose these pins so each set is one port; the ports from ArduinoCore-avr 1.8.8, variants/mega/pins_arduino.h (the pin to port table), https://github.com/arduino/ArduinoCore-avr/blob/1.8.8/variants/mega/pins_arduino.h

dir_pin_s0.rule: Axis 0's DIR to its driver: port C bit 0 (PC0); port C runs from D37 down to D30

body_width.rule: Board length, the 4.0 in outline the Mega is usually given; Arduino's datasheet (A000067) could not be read here: measure yours
body_width.source: The Mega 2560's usual 4.0 x 2.1 in outline; Arduino datasheet A000067 not read

body_depth.rule: Board width, 2.1 in, the Uno's width (the Uno's drawing reads 53.2 mm at its scale); measure yours
body_depth.source: Arduino UNO R3 datasheet (A000066), 5.4 Board Outline, for the shared 2.1 in width, https://docs.arduino.cc/resources/datasheets/A000066-datasheet.pdf

board_thickness.source: The common 1.6 mm FR-4 board; measure yours

pinout.value: D22..D29 STEP axes 0..7, D37..D30 DIR axes 0..7, A8..A15 home switches axes 0..7, D38 enable, D11 servo
pinout.rule: The Mega pins the streamer uses; see the rules for each pin
